brief: My courtyard is bright indirect with low moisture, and no pets live in the household. A bright but sunless courtyard with fast-draining gravel pots, purely decorative.

design.site_summary: A bright indirect courtyard with low moisture and fast-draining gravel pots, with no pets living in the household.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme is structured into three height layers: trailing shade-loving ferns on wall hooks at the vertical level, lush architectural foliage plants in mid-height containers against the back wall, and low-growing textural succulents and shade perennials spilling across the floor-level gravel pots.
design.combination_logic: The plants work together through a strong contrast of fine textures, glossy fronds, and matte succulent rosettes. The vertical ferns provide soft, weeping motion that draws the eye upward, the mid-layer broad-leaved plants anchor the walls with rich green structural weight, and the ground-level stonecrop and ivy act as a cohesive, low-maintenance carpet that unifies the fast-draining gravel aesthetic.

zones.placement: On high wall-mounted hooks, receiving bright indirect ambient light from the open courtyard sky with no direct sun.

plants.why: Thrives in bright indirect light and adds lush, weeping vertical volume.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes soft, fine-textured weeping fronds that break the rigid lines of the courtyard walls and contrast sharply with the stiff foliage below.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top two inches of potting mix feel dry, approximately once a week.
Mist the fronds bi-weekly to maintain ambient humidity.
Remove any brown or dead fronds at the base as needed.

zones.placement: In large wall planters at knee-to-waist height, positioned against the main courtyard wall in bright indirect light.

plants.why: Extremely resilient in low moisture and indirect light conditions.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides bold, upright, glossy dark green lance-shaped leaves that create a strong architectural anchor against the wall.

plants.why: Adapts well to bright indirect light and fast-draining gravel-topped potting media.
plants.role_in_combination: Offers a bright variegated contrast with arched linear leaves that soften the dark, glossy mass of the Cast Iron Plant.

maintenance: Allow the soil to dry out moderately between waterings to prevent root issues in the gravel medium.
Feed with a balanced liquid fertilizer once a month during spring and summer.
Repot every two to three years in fresh, well-draining potting mix.

zones.placement: In wide, shallow gravel-topped pots resting directly on the courtyard floor, receiving diffused indirect light from above.

plants.why: Thrives in fast-draining gravel pots and low moisture environments.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as a low, creeping green carpet that weaves between the larger pots, offering a fleshy, succulent leaf texture.

maintenance: Water sparingly, as this zone retains drought tolerance well in the gravel setup.
Trim back any creeping stems in early spring to keep the pots looking neat and contained.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture levels across all containers by inserting a finger into the gravel and topsoil.
care_instructions.frequency: Once a week in summer, every two weeks in autumn and winter

care_instructions.task: Apply a half-strength balanced liquid fertilizer to the mid-level structural pots to support steady foliage growth.
Inspect the Boston Fern and Cast Iron Plant for dust accumulation on leaves, wiping gently with a damp cloth.

care_cautions: Overwatering the Boston Fern in its vertical hanging basket can lead to root rot, especially since the courtyard lacks direct sun to quickly evaporate excess moisture.
The fast-draining gravel pots on the ground layer may dry out too quickly during unexpected warm spells, causing the Sedum makinoi to wrinkle if not checked.
design.pet_safety_note: As there are no pets living in the household, pet safety is not a limiting factor for this decorative shade scheme.
